text:

Ph.D. Student The University of Hong Kong
Email
CV






I am a Ph.D. student in the School of Future Media at the University of Hong Kong, supervised by Prof. King-wa Fu and Prof. Bin Chen.
My research focuses on digital journalism, political communication, and platform governance.
Previously, I received an M.A. from Tsinghua University (2025) and a B.A. from Zhejiang University (2022). I was also an exchange student at National Chengchi University in Taiwan (Fall 2024). I also worked as a journalism intern at Caixin Media and The Paper.





In Chinese

Li, Hongtao, Liu, Yusi, Dai, Fankai. (2026). Where’s the Covid-19 testing stations now? Liminal Memoryscape, and Covid-19 Heritage in China’s Urban Space. Communication & Society (TSSCI), 75, 1–36. [Publisher’s Version]
Zhou, Ruiming, Wang, Weijia, Dai, Fankai, & Zhou, Ziluo. (2021). Learning to make news: How Chinese college students and faculty covered the Covid-19 pandemic. Shanghai Journalism Review (CSSCI), 11, 53–65. [Publisher’s Version]





Dai, Fankai. (2025). Amusing ourselves or deliberating for justice? The impact of entertainment content and gamification on the quality of discussion in crowdsourced content moderation. Paper presented at the 75th Annual Conference of the International Communication Association (ICA), Denver, Colorado, USA.
Chen, Junyi, Dai, Fankai, & Mou, Yi. (2025). AI Fact-checking or Rumor-debunking? Assessing the Impact of Source, Genre Type, and Heuristic Thinking on Correction Credibility. Paper presented at the 75th Annual Conference of the International Communication Association (ICA), Denver, Colorado, USA.
Wang, Weijia, Dai, Fankai, Xing, Jianhong, & Seong Yun, Du. (2024). Double Generalized Hate Speech: The Boundary of Hate Speech in China’s Crowdsourcing Governance Practices. Paper presented at the International Association for Media and Communication Research (IAMCR) Annual Conference, Christchurch, New Zealand.
Dai, Fankai, Chen, Junyi. (2024). Fact-checking is fact-checking? A comparative analysis of four Chinese fact-checking organizations. Paper presented at the 74th Annual Conference of the International Communication Association (ICA), Gold Coast, Australia.
Zhou, Ruiming, Dai, Fankai, & Wang, Weijia. (2024). Regulatory talk: An informal coercing strategy governing the Internet in China. Paper presented at the 21st Chinese Internet Research Conference (CIRC 2024), Brisbane, Australia.





Email: fankaidai@connect.hku.hk
Address: Room 107, Eliot Hall, The University of Hong Kong, Pok Fu Lam, Hong Kong
